name: Disaster
definition: A large disruptive event collapses ordinary systems, forcing intersecting characters to respond under uncertainty while consequences spread across public and intimate scales.
negative_signals: oppressive future society without an acute event
diagnostic_questions: Does the event reorganize institutions and relationships?
Are response and aftermath as important as spectacle?

neighbors.distinction: Disaster emphasizes cascading collective disruption; survival emphasizes sustained material adaptation.
Disaster reduces an existing world through crisis, while dystopia elaborates an oppressive order.

reader_promises.name: Cascading consequence
reader_promises.description: Show one failure creating further failures across physical and social systems.

reader_promises.name: Human scale
reader_promises.description: Anchor large disruption in specific duties, separations, and moral choices.

roles.name: Responder
roles.description: Acts within or beyond a professional duty as systems fail.

roles.name: Separated person
roles.description: Turns the large event into a concrete route, promise, or reunion objective.

roles.name: Authority under strain
roles.description: Allocates information and resources while facing uncertainty and legitimacy pressure.

movements.name: Warning or rupture
movements.description: Establish normal dependencies and the first sign or impact of systemic failure.

movements.name: Cascade
movements.description: Let physical and institutional responses create new bottlenecks and dangers.

movements.name: Triage and convergence
movements.description: Bring objectives together through scarce time, routes, and care.

movements.name: Aftermath
movements.description: Resolve immediate danger and reveal responsibility, loss, and reconstruction.

complications.name: Secondary event
complications.description: An established vulnerability produces a new hazard after the first impact.

complications.name: Bad information
complications.description: Incomplete reports cause rational but harmful allocation decisions.

complications.name: Route conflict
complications.description: Saving one group blocks access or resources needed by another.

twists.name: Preventable scale
twists.description: The initiating event was unavoidable but its scale reflects prior choices or neglect.

twists.name: Unsafe refuge
twists.description: A designated safe location depends on a failing system already shown.

conclusions.name: Contained crisis
conclusions.description: The cascade is stopped through coordinated sacrifice and accumulated knowledge.

conclusions.name: Survival and accounting
conclusions.description: Immediate danger passes while responsibility and rebuilding remain contested.

conclusions.name: Transformed community
conclusions.description: The event permanently changes how people organize care, power, or memory.

subversions: Center maintenance workers and mutual aid rather than a lone savior.
Let a smaller preventable failure matter more than spectacular destruction.
cliches_to_avoid: Authorities who are irrational solely to delay rescue
quality_checks: Large stakes remain legible through specific people.
The aftermath addresses responsibility and changed systems.

sources.title: Not Death, but Annihilation
sources.author_or_organization: University of Washington Department of English
sources.contribution: Distinguishes catastrophe's world-reduction and personal cultural loss from dystopian world-building.

sources.title: The Cambridge Companion to Popular Fiction
sources.contribution: Frames bodily danger and suspense as repertoires that can mix with other genres.
